\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{غرور} (ghorur)}{غرور (ghorur)}]{\fa{غرور} (ghorur) — pride; vanity}

\label{lesson:FA-C480-ghorur}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for an invoice, then the Persian for a cash machine.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{غرور}}
\textbf{\fa{غرور}} (\emph{ghorur}) — \textquotedblleft{}pride; vanity\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{غرور} \fa{او} \fa{دوستانش} \fa{را} \fa{ناراحت} \fa{میکند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ghorur-e u dustânash râ nârâhat mikonad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
His pride upsets his friends.
\end{quote}

A noun, usually with a bad sense: too much pride. \emph{ghorur dâshtan} — to be vain.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ghorur} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{ġurūr}, which EtymDB glosses 'pride' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{مغرور} (maghrur)}{مغرور (maghrur)}]{\fa{مغرور} (maghrur) — arrogant; conceited}

\label{lesson:FA-C480-maghrur}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a cash machine, then the Persian for pride.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{مغرور}}
\textbf{\fa{مغرور}} (\emph{maghrur}) — \textquotedblleft{}arrogant; conceited\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{برادرش} \fa{خیلی} \fa{مغرور} \fa{است} \fa{و} \fa{به} \fa{کسی} \fa{سلام} \fa{نمیکند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{barâdarash kheyli maghrur ast va be kasi salâm nemikonad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Her brother is very arrogant and doesn't greet anyone.
\end{quote}

An adjective. \emph{maghrur shodan} — to become full of oneself.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{maghrur} comes from Arabic \emph{maġrūr} (EtymDB). It is usually linked with Arabic \emph{ġurūr}, 'pride', the source of \emph{ghorur}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{فروتن} (forutan)}{فروتن (forutan)}]{\fa{فروتن} (forutan) — humble, modest}

\label{lesson:FA-C480-forutan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for pride, then the Persian for arrogant.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{فروتن}}
\textbf{\fa{فروتن}} (\emph{forutan}) — \textquotedblleft{}humble, modest\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{با} \fa{اینکه} \fa{مشهور} \fa{است،} \fa{خیلی} \fa{فروتن} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u bâ inke mashhur ast, kheyli forutan ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Although he is famous, he is very humble.
\end{quote}

Praise, not blame. The noun is \emph{forutani} 'humility'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{forutan} is a native Persian compound, usually explained as \emph{foru}, 'down', and \emph{tan}, 'body': someone who bows low. EtymDB has no entry for it, so the analysis is hedged; it is not a loan.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{افتخار} \fa{کردن} (eftekhâr kardan)}{افتخار کردن (eftekhâr kardan)}]{\fa{افتخار} \fa{کردن} (eftekhâr kardan) — to be proud (of)}

\label{lesson:FA-C480-eftekhar-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for arrogant, then the Persian for humble.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{افتخار} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{افتخار} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{eftekhâr kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to be proud (of)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مادرم} \fa{به} \fa{موفقیت} \fa{من} \fa{افتخار} \fa{میکند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mâdaram be movaffaqiyat-e man eftekhâr mikonad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My mother is proud of my success.
\end{quote}

\emph{eftekhâr} 'pride, honour' + \emph{kardan} 'to do'; present stem \emph{kon-}. What you are proud of takes \emph{be}: \emph{be chizi eftekhâr kardan}. Unlike \emph{ghorur}, a good kind of pride.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{eftekhâr} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{iftiḫār}; EtymDB links it with Arabic \emph{faḫr}, 'honour, pride' (EtymDB). \emph{kardan}, 'to do', is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{eftekhâr kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{eftekhâr kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for arrogant, then the Persian for humble, then say \emph{eftekhâr kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{خودنمایی} \fa{کردن} (khodnamâyi kardan)}{خودنمایی کردن (khodnamâyi kardan)}]{\fa{خودنمایی} \fa{کردن} (khodnamâyi kardan) — to show off}

\label{lesson:FA-C480-khodnamayi-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for humble, then the Persian for to be proud.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{خودنمایی} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{خودنمایی} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{khodnamâyi kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to show off\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{جلوی} \fa{دوستانش} \fa{خودنمایی} \fa{میکند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u jelo-ye dustânash khodnamâyi mikonad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He shows off in front of his friends.
\end{quote}

\emph{khod} 'self' + \emph{namâyi} 'showing' (stem \emph{namâ-}, from \emph{namudan} 'to show') + \emph{kardan}. Present: \emph{khodnamâyi mikonad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{khodnamâyi} is built on native Persian parts: \emph{khod}, 'self', and \emph{namâ-}, the present stem of \emph{namudan}, 'to show', with the noun ending \emph{-i}: showing oneself. \emph{kardan}, 'to do', turns it into a verb; none of it is borrowed.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{khodnamâyi kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for humble, then the Persian for to be proud, then say \emph{khodnamâyi kardan} again
\end{itemize}
